clue.text: Being forced to work from Pole to point

parts.note: a Pole, a native of Poland, is a Slav
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone is driven to labour across the whole map, from the Pole to the furthest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a geographical pole, but it is a Polish person, one of the Slavs.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave is a human being compelled to toil without pay or freedom.

clue.text: Protection from what could be hell under a heater

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the shuffled piece below the heater word

parts.note: the sun heats the earth

indicators.note: what could be means the letters of the word for hell can be rearranged

parts.note: Hades is the underworld, hell

explanation.surface: Something guards against the hellish heat beneath a radiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be' rearranges HADES, a name for hell, into SHADE, which sits 'under' SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is a parasol or awning that shields one from strong sunlight.

clue.text: Make a cat sit in an unstable position

indicators.note: make is read as form or fashion, building something new from the letters of a cat sit

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a cat to sit while it wobbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' rearranges A CAT SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatic describes something without stability, not tending to stay in one position.

clue.text: Island the reverse of 10 not unwanted

indicators.note: the reverse of says the remaining letters are read backwards
unwanted says the word not is thrown out of the other answer

parts.note: 10 refers to the answer to 10 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: An island's name is the opposite of some earlier clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwanted' removes NOT from NOTABLE (10 across), leaving ABLE; 'the reverse of' turns it round to name the island of Napoleon's exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is a Mediterranean isle off Tuscany.

clue.text: Specific measures for conscience

explanation.surface: Exact measurements are taken for one's moral sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruple is an old apothecaries' weight of twenty grains; scruples are also moral qualms, the workings of a conscience.

clue.text: Positive triumph for resolved veracity in court, albeit non-U

indicators.note: resolved is read as broken down and reconstituted, the letters reworked
non-U says the letter U is to be left out of the words

explanation.surface: Truth wins out in a law court, though not in an upper-class way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'albeit non-U' removes the U from VERACITY IN COURT, and 'resolved' rearranges the remaining fourteen letters. Non-U is British slang for not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A certain victory is a win that is sure, beyond doubt.

clue.text: Crumpled suit in the Outer Hebrides

indicators.note: crumpled tells us the letters of suit are crushed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A creased suit is worn on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumpled' rearranges SUIT. The Outer Hebrides are islands off north-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Uist (North and South) is an island group in the Scottish Western Isles.

clue.text: The old king's entrance to St Paul's?

definitions.text: The old king's entrance to St Paul's?

parts.note: Lud is a legendary ancient king of Britain
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch's doorway leads to the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludgate was a gate in London's old wall, said to be named after King Lud; Ludgate Hill climbs to St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludgate was a western gateway of the City of London, on the route up to St Paul's.

clue.text: Become sickly on Sunday, say

parts.note: to peak is an old verb meaning to waste away or look ill, as in peaky

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill on the Sabbath, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak is to utter words, to say something.

clue.text: Engineered marriage-what's holding it up?

parts.note: engineered describes something mechanical, technical
getting hitched is slang for marrying, so a hitch is a marriage

explanation.surface: A contrived wedding is delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding it up' means delaying it, not supporting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical hitch is a mechanical fault causing a delay.

clue.text: Well known but obliged to eat off the floor?

definitions.text: obliged to eat off the floor?

explanation.surface: A famous person reduced to dining on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means famous or eminent; read as two words it says there is no furniture to dine at, so food goes on the floor.

clue.text: What's left is the wrong side in a way across the Channel

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the French street word

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way in France across the English Channel

indicators.note: wrong tells us the letters of side are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Leftovers come from being on the wrong side of a road in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes ESID from SIDE, and 'in' puts that inside RUE, the French word for street.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder after the main part has gone.

clue.text: Strong dislike of two articles replaced

indicators.note: replaced says the letters of the two little words are put back in a new order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone loathes two items that were swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges A and THE, the two English articles, into a four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate is intense loathing, a strong dislike.

clue.text: Salesman with a bargain for a motorist?

parts.note: a bargain is low-priced, cheap
a jack lifts a car, a tool for a motorist

explanation.surface: A car dealer offers a motorist a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: A cheapjack is a hawker selling inferior goods at low prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapjack is a pedlar or street seller of shoddy wares.

clue.text: See 13
Returned as a spirit in old Salisbury

indicators.note: returned says the little word as is turned back

parts.note: taken as written
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A ghost came back to haunt historic Salisbury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost, but it is a drink. Sarum is the old name of Salisbury, an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarum is the historic Latin-derived name of Salisbury in Wiltshire.

clue.text: Place for higher class pupils

parts.note: read as a school grouping of the senior pupils, not a posh establishment

explanation.surface: A school for the well-to-do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'higher class' suggests social class; it means a more senior school class.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the senior year groups are called the upper forms.

clue.text: At any rate, one of the slowest stenographer could cope with

definitions.text: At any rate, one of the slowest stenographer could cope with

parts.words: At any rate, one of the slowest stenographer could cope with
parts.note: rate is literal: the pace of spoken words that even the slowest shorthand writer can keep up with

explanation.surface: Grudgingly, a poor shorthand typist could manage something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At any rate' looks like the phrase meaning 'anyway', but it is about rate as speed of words per minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictation speed is the pace at which text is read out for a stenographer to take down.

clue.text: Indeed not all went

indicators.note: in places the partial piece inside the word deed

parts.note: taken as written
a part is not all of something

explanation.surface: Indeed, some of them left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' splits into 'In deed': PART goes 'In' DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed means left or went away.

clue.text: The grammatical objective of indictable content?

explanation.surface: The aim of grammar is compared with material fit for a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The accusative case marks a sentence's direct object in grammar; read literally it is a lawsuit whose content is an accusation.

clue.text: Looped nautical rope Tom put his foot in?

explanation.surface: A tomcat steps in a coil of ship's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-paw is a sailor's hitch with two loops; read literally it is a tomcat's foot.

clue.text: A strange mortal feeling half-dead

indicators.note: strange says the letters of mortal are in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd human being feels near death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges MORTAL after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alamort, from French à la mort, means dispirited or nearly lifeless.

clue.text: Scraps for horses

explanation.surface: Leftover food is given to horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bits are small pieces; bits are also the metal mouthpieces of a horse's bridle.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill's first and only son

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the name

parts.note: only suggests one, the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Buffalo Bill had just one boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffalo Bill' looks like the showman, but 'Buffalo' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is the animal popularly called the American buffalo.

clue.text: Sound of fire in the channel

indicators.note: sound of says the word for fire is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: Gunfire is heard echoing in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' is the verb, as with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a sloping trough or channel down which things slide.

clue.text: Silence a follower slightly crazy

indicators.note: follower tells us the letter a comes behind the word for silence

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

explanation.surface: A disciple is told to keep quiet, being a bit unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for mildly mad or senile.

clue.text: Understanding fish

explanation.surface: Someone grasps what a fish is.
explanation.definitionFit: The sole of the foot is what one stands on, an under-standing; the sole is also a flatfish.

clue.text: See 16
Bolster up in an athletic pastime

indicators.note: in places the word up inside the pastime word

parts.note: a sport is an athletic pastime
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coach props someone up during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce.

clue.text: Tour round to dig up truffles, perhaps

annotationWithheld.why: 'Tour round to dig up truffles, perhaps' (ROOT OUT): TOUR + TO give six letters; the seventh, O, can only come from 'round', which is also the only anagram indicator, a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Tour round to dig up truffles, perhaps

clue.text: Place to resettle when idle

indicators.note: to resettle means the letters of when idle are moved into a new setting

explanation.surface: Someone out of work decides where to move house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resettle' rearranges WHEN IDLE into the Indian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is a city, the capital of India.

clue.text: Wed after a final check

explanation.surface: A couple marry after a last inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Mated means paired or coupled; in chess a king is mated after the final, unanswerable check.
